name: karea
description: Shows whether your active Karea task is in sync with what this session did: hint-line chip, behind band, changed-in-Karea alerts, task pane, sync receipts, a /ksync command and the Karea skill

apiKey.title: Karea API key
apiKey.description: Optional. Leave empty to use your connected Karea MCP server (karea or claude.ai Karea). A key gives exact change history (who changed what) instead of comparing snapshots.

mcpServer.title: Karea MCP server name
mcpServer.description: Leave empty to try 'karea' then 'claude.ai Karea'. Set it if your Karea server is named differently in /mcp.

preset.title: Commands that count as progress
preset.description: git: successful commits and pushes only. general: also PRs, deploys, migrations. salesforce: also sf deploys and data loads. both: all of them. Each is counted only when its output shows it succeeded.

extraPatterns.title: Extra progress patterns
extraPatterns.description: Your own commands, as label=regex pairs separated by ';'. Example: released=\bmake release\b

detectDecisions.title: Spot decisions and open questions
detectDecisions.description: Off by default. When on, after each reply a small Haiku call (billed to your account) reads the exchange to spot decisions about the task or open questions, and flags them as not synced.

pollSeconds.title: Check Karea every (seconds)
pollSeconds.description: How often to look for changes made in Karea while you are active. 300 (5 minutes) is recommended; lower values mean more Karea calls. Minimum 60.

receipts.title: Sync receipts
receipts.description: Print a one-line receipt in the transcript after each Karea write.

statusFile.title: Write the chip to a file
statusFile.description: Also write the status chip to ~/.claude/karea/status-<session id> so your own status line script can show it.

questionMeeting.title: Meeting for new open questions
questionMeeting.description: When Claude creates an open question: leave empty to be asked each time which upcoming meeting to link it to; 'none' to never link one; or part of a meeting's title (e.g. your daily's name) to always link the next occurrence of that meeting that has not started yet, preferring one in the question's project.
